title: Ops Toolbelt Unified Surface (OTUS) + Runbook->Task Compiler
creator: Priya Patel
description:
Goal: Ship a single developer-facing surface (OTUS) to discover, execute, and safely replay admin utilities and runbooks-as-tasks. Deliver a compile-time flow that converts vetted runbook fragments into typed, idempotent tasks with RBAC gates and an optional dry-run/replay harness. Rationale: current runbook tooling is fragmented (scripts, ad-hoc snippets, and untyped playlets). OTUS will reduce context-switching for oncall, provide reproducible automation, and enable incremental automation without losing human-in-the-loop safety.

Scope:
- A registry for admin utilities (plugin metadata, semantic versioning, compatibility matrix).
- Runbook->Task Compiler that ingests canonical runbook snippets (markdown+frontmatter) and emits typed task descriptors (JSON schema + CLI shim).
- Replay harness that can safely execute tasks in dry-run mode and record deterministic inputs/outputs for later re-run.
- RBAC & approval hooks integrated with existing IAM prototypes (approve-for-exec tokens).
- Telemetry: unit-level success/failure, duration, RBAC denials, and intent-extraction confidence.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Two existing runbooks (DB-rotate-keys, Node-evict) compiled into task descriptors and validated in staging.
2) OTUS UI (basic) lists registered utilities and shows version history + compatibility.
3) Replay harness can run a compiled task in dry-run mode and produce identical telemetry traces to a normal run.
4) RBAC gating prevents exec for a canned test user without approval.
5) Integration tests + end-to-end smoke pass in staging and are wired to CI.

Design decisions / trade-offs:
- Compiler output uses JSON Schema for task parameter typing (balances expressivity and easier validation).
- We will not try to auto-quantize side-effects (e.g., rolling restarts) — instead we require an explicit safe-mode flag on tasks.
- Chosen model for runbook ingest: frontmatter metadata with canonical steps rather than free-form natural language parsing to limit automation surprises.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1: Implement registry and publishing flow; compile 2 pilot runbooks.
- Week 2: Wire RBAC hooks and replay harness; run manual smoke tests with SRE.
- Week 3: Add telemetry & CI jobs; run canary with oncall volunteers.
- Post-release: iterate on liveness/observability, add more runbook patterns, and prepare a migration script for legacy snippets.

Testing & safety:
- All compiled tasks must pass a sandboxed dry-run that verifies non-mutating execution traces.
- Canary policy: initial exec permission restricted to oncall+owner group, escalated after two weeks with zero safety incidents.

Notes on implementation:
- Compiler will be implemented as a small Rust binary (fast validation, deterministic output).
- Registry metadata stored in ops-toolbelt postgres schema; UI served from console-2025.03 under /admin/otus.
- Replay harness will use existing admin sandbox infra (ENG-271444) and augment it to snapshot sidecar state.

PRs / artifacts: see links above.
